basis: Developmental encephalopathy with seizures and intellectual disability in 10/10; hypotonia and movement abnormalities are neurologic manifestations.
Malignant bone-forming tumour arising in bone; possible pulmonary metastases do not establish common lung involvement.
Inherited tryptophan metabolism disorders; no additional organ injury is established across this heterogeneous group.
Defining prenatal bone fragility, microcephaly with brain developmental abnormalities, and bilateral cataracts; cardiac defects are occasional.
Defining intellectual disability/epilepsy, hypotrichosis, and brachydactyly with epiphyseal abnormalities; joint dislocations are very frequent.
Immunodeficiency with autoimmunity; Crohn disease and asthma are separate diagnoses. Bronchiectasis may follow infections; microcytic anemia does not establish direct blood-cell injury.
Immune response to inhaled antigens directly causes chronic pulmonary inflammation and fibrosis.
Muscular dystrophy with spinal contractures; cardiac conduction abnormalities frequent (30-79%). Respiratory insufficiency reflects respiratory muscle weakness rather than direct lung injury.
Psychiatric eating disorder; secondary dental, gastrointestinal or electrolyte complications are not defining organ disease.
Glycosylation disorder with developmental encephalopathy; hearing loss frequent (30-79%; 2/2). Visual impairment may be central; gastric bleeding frequency is unclear.
Renal tubular atrophy and interstitial fibrosis cause kidney failure; hepatic fibrosis occurs in 6/53, below the involvement threshold.
Infantile interstitial lung disease with persistent tachypnea and hypoxemia; chest wall abnormalities occur in only 22%.
Manganese transport disorder with dystonia (14/15) and defining polycythemia; direct hepatic injury with cirrhosis in 5/6. Four-axis cap reached.
Acute altitude-related cerebral dysfunction defines this syndrome; pulmonary edema and cerebral edema are distinct severe altitude illnesses, not routine involvement.
Defined autoimmune immune-dysregulation disorder; supplied evidence does not identify common direct injury to a specific nonimmune organ.
Cerebellar degeneration causes ataxia, tremor and cognitive impairment; abnormal eye movements and dysphagia reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Cerebellar and extrapyramidal disorder with cognitive impairment; nystagmus and abnormal saccades do not establish intrinsic ocular injury.
Carcinoma arising in the submandibular salivary gland, which belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Otosclerosis damages auditory function through abnormal otic bone remodeling; this localized ear disorder does not establish generalized skeletal disease.
Ischemic pituitary necrosis causes hormone deficiencies; reported visual-field abnormalities lack localization to direct ocular injury. Anemia and skin changes are secondary endocrine effects.
Scleral inflammation is usually immune-mediated; infectious forms also meet the mechanism axis. Associated systemic diseases are separate diagnoses.
Defining polysyndactyly and complex cardiac malformations; hepatic ductal plate malformation frequent (30-79%). Renal and ocular abnormalities are occasional.
Adenocarcinoma originating in the urinary bladder, included in the renal axis.
HTLV-1-associated chronic infective eczema; chronic crusting rhinitis is a major diagnostic feature and the nose belongs to pulmonary. Later leukemia and myelopathy are excluded.
Benign tumour occupying the hypopharynx; the pharynx belongs to the pulmonary axis.
